claim: The grafana-cli path applies the new proxy_token with no feature-flag check (OpenFeature is never initialized there), so the CLI switches tokens regardless of whether the toggle is enabled while the server does not.
raw: There is no flag check here, and OpenFeature is never initialized in the `grafana-cli plugins install` path (`runPluginCommand` bypasses server DI entirely). So the moment an operator writes `proxy_token` into their config, `grafana-cli plugins install` starts authenticating with the dedicated token **regardless of whether ... [the flag] is enabled**, while the server keeps using the SSO token.

claim: The new toggle is resolved once at boot but its registry entry lacks RequiresRestart: true, so operators using a dynamic/remote provider will believe flipping it takes effect at runtime when it does not.
raw: **2. The flag is evaluated exactly once at startup, but is not marked `RequiresRestart`.** ... this flag *looks* runtime-flippable to whoever operates it, but flipping it does nothing until a restart — and once resolved off, the configured dedicated token is gone from the field entirely. `RequiresRestart: true` is an established convention in this registry (51 occurrences of the field).

claim: Token resolution is wired per-entrypoint rather than at config construction, and the test-server entrypoints (testinfra.go, pluginsintegration/test_helper.go) never call ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken, silently yielding an empty token instead of the SSO token.
raw: `server.InitializeForTest` (wire_gen.go:1073) calls `pluginconfig.ProvidePluginManagementConfig`, which now reads `cfg.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken` — but `testinfra.go` initializes OpenFeature at line 124 and never calls `ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken`. Same for `test_helper.go:45`. In those paths a `sso_api_token` ... now yields an **empty** token instead of the SSO token, and the failure is silent

claim: The docs name the feature toggle as dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken while the registered name is grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken, so following the docs will not enable the feature.
raw: **4. Documented feature-toggle name is wrong — users cannot enable the feature by following the docs.** ... The registered name is `grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` (`pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:2253`). Dotted names are used verbatim in `[feature_toggles] enable = ...`, so the documented name will simply not match anything.

claim: The documentation for proxy_token never mentions the sso_api_token fallback, omitting the most operationally important behavior of the key.
raw: And the doc never mentions the `sso_api_token` fallback, which is the single most important thing an operator needs to know about this key.

claim: The install-command test still asserts GcomToken(), a method no longer used by plugin installs, so it validates dead code and nothing covers the CLI's new token-fallback logic.
raw: `install_command_test.go:103` still asserts `c.GcomToken()` — a method that no longer participates in plugin installs after `install_command.go:102` switched to `c.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken()`. The integration test now validates dead code, and nothing covers the CLI's new fallback logic. `testinfra.GrafanaOpts` has no `proxy_token` option, so this case isn't even expressible today.

claim: No test asserts that ProvidePluginManagementConfig or ProxyGnetRequest actually carry the resolved token, leaving both production consumption paths uncovered.
raw: Nothing asserts that `ProvidePluginManagementConfig` or `ProxyGnetRequest` carry the resolved token. `pkg/api` has no `grafana_com_proxy_test.go` at all (pre-existing), but `ProvidePluginManagementConfig` is trivially testable and the field swap at `pluginconfig/config.go:39` is exactly the kind of one-line change a future refactor could silently revert.

claim: GcomToken() is now dead in production yet retained in three places alongside a near-identical method with subtly different semantics, with no comment explaining why.
raw: **6. `GcomToken()` is now dead in production but retained in three places.** `command_line.go:29,101`, `command_line_mock.go:149`, `upgrade_command_test.go:133`. Its only remaining caller is a test. Two nearly-identical methods on the same interface with subtly different semantics is a trap for the next person. Either delete it or add a comment stating it is retained only for X.

claim: The flag name is a hardcoded string literal in pkg/setting instead of the typed featuremgmt constant, so a registry-only rename would silently evaluate a nonexistent flag that defaults to false.
raw: **7. The flag name is a hardcoded string literal in `pkg/setting`.** `setting.go:763` cannot use `featuremgmt.FlagGrafanaDedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` because `featuremgmt` imports `setting`. ... a registry-only rename would leave this literal silently evaluating a nonexistent flag (which returns the `false` default — indistinguishable from "flag off").

claim: conf/sample.ini was not updated with the new proxy_token key (and defaults.ini gained it without a comment), breaking the convention of keeping both files in sync.
raw: **8. `conf/sample.ini` was not updated.** `conf/sample.ini:1815-1819` documents `[grafana_com] sso_api_token` with an explanatory comment but has no `proxy_token` entry. `defaults.ini` gained the key without a comment. Grafana convention is to keep both in sync.

claim: A new [grafana_com] test was placed in the test file devoted to [plugins] settings, residue from the abandoned [plugins] install_token design.
raw: **9. New `grafana_com` test placed in the plugins settings test file.** `pkg/setting/setting_plugins_test.go:284` defines `Test_readGrafanaComSettings_GrafanaComProxyAPIToken` in a file otherwise devoted to `[plugins]`. Residue from the abandoned `[plugins] install_token` design.

claim: The new grafana_com settings test covers only the environment-variable path and not the ini-key path.
raw: Also, it only covers the env-var path, not the ini-key path.

claim: toggles_gen.json permanently records tombstones for four phantom flag names that never existed on main, because the generator derives history from the branch's rename commits.
raw: **10. `toggles_gen.json` carries three tombstones for names that never existed on `main`.** ... gains `pluginsDedicatedInstallToken`, `dedicatedGnetProxyToken`, `dedicatedGrafanaComProxyToken` and `dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken`, each with a `deletionTimestamp` ... it permanently records four phantom flags in a tracked file. Worth a squash of the toggle-rename commits if that's cheap.

claim: The new doc line is the only relref shortcode in the file, contradicting the repo style guide's instruction to use inline Markdown links.
raw: **11. Docs use a `relref` shortcode against local style, with a likely-wrong anchor.** `docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md:2325` is the *only* `relref` in this ~3000-line file, and `docs/AGENTS.md:110` says "Use inline Markdown links".

claim: The doc link's anchor is probably wrong: sibling headings render underscores as dashes, so #feature_toggles should likely be #feature-toggles.
raw: Additionally, the sibling cross-reference at line 2309 renders `### [grafana_com]` as `#grafana-com` (underscore → dash), which suggests `#feature_toggles` should be `#feature-toggles`. [Inference — I could not build the docs site to confirm the anchor generation rule.]

claim: A mockery-generated DO NOT EDIT file was hand-edited: the added block lacks the comment mockery emits, so regenerating the mock will now produce a diff.
raw: **12. `command_line_mock.go` is a mockery `DO NOT EDIT` file that was hand-edited.** The added block at line 162 lacks the `// X provides a mock function with given fields:` comment mockery emits. It is consistent with the existing hand-edited `GcomToken` block above it, so this is pre-existing drift rather than new — but regenerating the mock will now produce a diff.
